items.text: Its members vote to keep in place the existing system, in which public health coverage is guaranteed to older, disabled, and low-income residents, most others rely on employer or subsidized private insurance, and about 8 percent of residents have no coverage.

Its members vote to keep in place the existing income support, in which mandatory pension schemes replace about 51 percent of an average worker's net earnings, unemployment benefits replace about 35 percent of an average earner's net income in the second month out of work, and a single adult with no other income is guaranteed about 6 percent of the median income, housing support included.
Co-led a letter, joined by 208 legislators, telling the chamber's leader to drop any legislation that would cut the public pension or public health coverage for older or low-income residents.

items.text: A former chair of the group introduced, with more than 100 cosponsors, a bill to enroll every resident in a single public health plan with no premiums, deductibles, or copayments.
Held a public hearing to build support for the single public health plan bill, where its chair called passing that bill one of the group's top priorities.
